messages:
nina: quick sync 1: prod alert: tenant with geo-restrictions saw writes rejected after active-active steering flipped the serving shard. client kept same session id but the selected model shard was now in a non-resident region. legal guard dropped it. anyone seen this pattern?
kyle: saw similar in canary when steering rebalanced by load. session->shard mapping didn't carry a region assertion.
dani: is this basically drift between routing layer and shard placement? active-active makes it worse because shards can be promoted in multiple regions.
henry: yup. two rough fixes: 1) make routing carry an immutable claim about the allowed region (token), or 2) make the serving shard carry accept-list for sessions. both have tradeoffs.
nina: my preference: issue a short-lived "region-assertion token" at session creation that the routing and serving layers both validate. token says allowed_region=* and expires. prevents blind steering.
kyle: questions: who mints tokens, how often, and what's the perf hit for verifying on each request?
dani: control-plane mints signed tokens (ed25519) on session create and on explicit handoff. proxy/serving validate locally; add small LRU cache per-session to avoid repeated verifies. TTL short (1-3m) to allow safe handoffs.
henry: edge case: what if a serving shard moves region (reschedule) mid-ttl? token would mismatch and we either deny or force a handback. need a runbook for operator-initiated move.
nina: agree. policy choices: default-deny on mismatch (safer, legal-friendly) vs default-allow-with-audit (higher availability). propose cluster-level config: EU clusters default-deny, others default-log-then-allow.
kyle: perf: ed25519 verify ~ microseconds but at high QPS caching needed. also we need key distribution to all serving nodes with overlap windows for rotation.
dani: got it. implement public-key pull, and accept previous keys during overlap. also include signature version in token to simplify lookup.
henry: alternative architecture: keep routing deterministic by session-key -> shard hashing so handoffs are explicit and never implicit. downside: reduces our ability to rebalance quickly.
nina: tradeoff note: deterministic pinning helps stability but hurts autoscaling. token approach keeps autoscale but enforces residency.
kyle: telemetry we want: token_verify_fail, token_region_mismatch, token_issue_rate, handoff_fallback_count. alert when mismatch rate > 0.05% over 5m.
dani: short-term mitigations: 1) add a safety check that prevents steering a session to a non-resident shard when tenant has strict_geo flag, 2) run a log-only canary for tokens for 48h.
nina: action items: Nina -> draft RFC "region-assertion token" (sequence diagrams + token format + TTL recommendations); Kyle -> spike verify library + small LRU cache in proxy (2d); Dani -> spec control-plane minting API and key-rotation plan; Henry -> ops runbook for forced handbacks and cluster policy defaults. I'll open the canary dashboard tile for token_region_mismatch metrics. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Canary note: steering canary on staging-4 produced 0.07% region_mismatch events; automatic rollback triggered for that canary run.
ning: thanks all, will post RFC link in this thread in 48h.
